new_abstractions: One collapsed terminal-launch view in grill.py — justified because two guards independently mis-read the same ledger, and a shared view is what stops them diverging again
current_flow: Every launch appends three rows to the delegation ledger: starting, then running, then a terminal row — confirmed against the live ledger, where all twelve grill launches are ('starting','running','succeeded'). _rounds_since_last_pass (grill.py:293) builds a SET of launch_ids from raw rows with no status filter at all, so any launch counts. _refuse_a_second_cold_read (grill.py:386) drops rows whose launch_status is 'failed', which looks like it excludes a failed launch but does not: that launch's starting and running rows are not failed, still carry its id, and the guard still refuses. Neither guard collapses rows per launch, so neither can act on how a launch actually ended.

summary: Three cold reads, and each cut the task rather than growing it. Read one found the escalation grant unbuildable here — open_escalation returns the first unspent record globally, the record carries no gate, the CLI has only --task — so it split to T5. Read two found the outcome field unbuildable as designed: the launcher runs the companion with --json, so stdout is a serialized object and the griller's CONVERGED marker never ends it; that deferred as D-0032 with a revisit trigger, and the confirmed spec was amended to stop promising it. Read three found the remaining premise wrong: the repeat-read guard does NOT already ignore failed launches, because row-level filtering cannot, so copying its filter to the cap would have fixed nothing. T2 is now one collapsed view consumed by both guards. The owner ruled both get fixed.
gaps: The plan still described the answered/interrupted design in its Technical Approach, its acceptance summary and T5's dependency line, after only the T2 bullet had been narrowed.
contradictions: The contract claimed the repeat-read guard already ignored failed launches and proposed copying that filter to the cap; the filter is row-level and a failed launch's starting and running rows defeat it, so both guards were broken and the proposed fix was a no-op.
resolutions: Both guards move to one view that collapses rows by launch_id to the latest, and a launch is failed only when THAT row is failed.
Required tests seed real lifecycles — starting/running/failed and starting/running/succeeded, plus standalone starting and running — rather than synthetic single rows.
The plan's Technical Approach, acceptance summary and T5 dependency were rewritten to match; T5 now depends on the collapsed view rather than on an outcome field that will not exist.
The owner ruled that T2 fixes BOTH guards, accepting that a failed launch will no longer block a retry without --reread.
